question: Come funziona GET /me?

context.heading: Retry flow
context.content:
A delivery in `rejected` state is retried only if the provider reported a
retryable error code. Retries create a new `deliveries` row with an incremented
`attempt_number`. A `bounced` delivery is never retried.

context.heading: Rate limiting
context.content:
`rateLimit.defaultRps` is 50 requests per second per caller.
`rateLimit.burst` is 100. `rateLimit.redisUrl` is required; without it the
gateway refuses to start.

context.heading: Upstream errors
context.content:
`upstream_timeout` (HTTP 504) when the upstream exceeds the route timeout.
`upstream_unavailable` (HTTP 502) when the connection fails. The gateway never
converts an upstream 5xx into a 2xx: upstream status codes above 499 are passed
through unchanged, with the body replaced by the gateway error envelope.

context.heading: GET /me
context.content:
Returns the authenticated user. The route requires a valid bearer token and is
handled by `UserController.getMe`, which calls `UserService.getCurrentUser`.
The response body is:

```json
{
  "id": "uuid",
  "email": "user@example.com",
  "displayName": "Ada Lovelace",
  "avatarUrl": "https://cdn.acme.dev/avatars/ada.png",
  "locale": "en-GB",
  "status": "active"
}
```

`displayName`, `avatarUrl` and `locale` come from the profile record. `id`,
`email` and `status` come from the account record.

context.heading: Current User Flow
context.content:
1. The client calls `GET /me` with a bearer token.
2. `authMiddleware` verifies the token and sets `req.auth.userId`.
3. `UserController.getMe` calls `UserService.getCurrentUser(userId)`.
4. `UserService` loads the account through `UserRepository.findById`.
5. `UserService` loads profile fields through `ProfileService.getProfile`.
6. The two records are merged into `CurrentUser` and serialised.

If the profile row is missing, step 5 returns the default profile, so
`displayName` falls back to the email local part.

context.heading: Provider errors
context.content:
`StripeGateway` translates provider failures into `ProviderCardError`,
`ProviderRateLimited` and `ProviderUnavailable`. `ProviderCardError` is final:
the attempt is recorded and no retry is scheduled. `ProviderRateLimited` and
`ProviderUnavailable` are retryable and consume one of the
`PAYMENT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` attempts.

answer:
`GET /me` restituisce l'utente autenticato e richiede un bearer token valido.

Percorso documentato:
- `authMiddleware` verifica il token e imposta `req.auth.userId` [05-main-flows.md — Current User Flow]
- `UserController.getMe` chiama `UserService.getCurrentUser(userId)` [04-api-reference.md — GET /me]
- `UserService` carica l'account con `UserRepository.findById` e i campi di profilo con `ProfileService.getProfile`, poi unisce i due record in `CurrentUser` [05-main-flows.md — Current User Flow]

Nel payload `id`, `email` e `status` provengono dal record account, mentre `displayName`, `avatarUrl` e `locale` provengono dal record di profilo [04-api-reference.md — GET /me].

question: Come funziona l'autenticazione?

context.heading: POST /providers/callbacks/{provider}
context.content:
Endpoint used by delivery providers to report status changes. Handled by
`DeliveryStatusListener`. The payload is provider specific and normalised into
the `deliveries.status` values.

context.heading: UpstreamProxy
context.content:
`UpstreamProxy` performs the forwarded call. It applies the per-route timeout,
retries idempotent methods and records the upstream latency metric
`gateway_upstream_duration_seconds`.

context.heading: Purpose
context.content:
DocSync generates, signs and delivers documents (contracts, certificates,
policy files) to end users. It is a Java 21 Spring Boot service. Documents are
produced from templates, stored in object storage and delivered through one of
several delivery providers.

context.heading: POST /auth/login
context.content:
Accepts `{ email, password }`. On success returns `{ accessToken, refreshToken,
expiresIn }` with HTTP 200. On invalid credentials returns HTTP 401 with body
`{ "error": "invalid_credentials" }`. The route is rate limited to 10 attempts
per email per 15 minutes.

context.heading: Authentication flow
context.content:
Every protected route passes through `authMiddleware`. The middleware reads the
`Authorization: Bearer <token>` header, verifies the RS256 signature, checks the
`exp` claim and loads the account id from the `sub` claim. It then attaches
`req.auth = { userId, scopes }`. Routes never parse the token themselves.

context.heading: AuthService
context.content:
`AuthService` verifies credentials, issues access and refresh tokens and
revokes sessions. It depends on `UserRepository` to load the account and on
`SessionRepository` to persist refresh tokens. Token signing uses the RS256 key
pair loaded at boot from the secret store.

context.heading: documents
context.content:
`documents` holds `id`, `request_id`, `storage_key`, `checksum_sha256`,
`signed`, `size_bytes`, `created_at`. One row per successfully rendered
artefact.

answer:
L'autenticazione è basata su token bearer firmati RS256.

- Le credenziali arrivano a `POST /auth/login` con `{ email, password }`; in caso di successo la rotta restituisce `accessToken`, `refreshToken` ed `expiresIn` con HTTP 200, altrimenti HTTP 401 `invalid_credentials` [04-api-reference.md — POST /auth/login].
- `AuthService` verifica le credenziali, emette access e refresh token e li firma con la coppia di chiavi RS256 caricata all'avvio dal secret store [02-architecture.md — AuthService].
- Ogni rotta protetta passa da `authMiddleware`, che legge l'header `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, verifica la firma RS256, controlla il claim `exp` e ricava l'id account dal claim `sub`, impostando `req.auth = { userId, scopes }` [02-architecture.md — Authentication flow].

Le rotte non fanno mai il parsing del token per conto proprio [02-architecture.md — Authentication flow].

context.content:
Database columns are snake_case. The API layer maps them to camelCase; the
mapping lives in `UserRepository.toDomain` and `ProfileRepository.toDomain`.
`display_name` in the database is `displayName` in the API payload.

context.content:
`documents.signed` is false only if the signing step was skipped, which happens

question: Quale tabella contiene i dati del profilo?

context.heading: Request pipeline
context.content:
Each request passes through the pipeline in order: `TLSTerminator`,
`RequestIdMiddleware`, `AuthMiddleware`, `RateLimiter`, `RouteResolver`,
`UpstreamProxy`. A middleware that rejects a request short circuits the rest of
the pipeline.

context.heading: templates
context.content:
`templates` holds `code` (primary key), `version`, `engine`, `body`,
`active`. Only rows with `active = true` can be resolved by `RenderService`.

context.heading: A provider was never called
context.content:
`ProviderRouter` rejects a delivery before calling any provider when the channel
has no mapping in `docsync.channels`. In that case the delivery is recorded with
`unsupported_channel` and no `provider_message_id` is present.

context.heading: user_profiles table
context.content:
The `user_profiles` table holds profile data: `user_id` (uuid, primary key and
foreign key to `users.id`), `display_name`, `avatar_url`, `locale`, `timezone`,
`updated_at`. There is exactly one profile row per account, created lazily on
first profile write.

context.heading: invoices
context.content:
`invoices` holds `id`, `subscription_id`, `number`, `currency`, `amount_cents`,
`status`, `issued_at`, `due_at`, `pdf_url`. `status` is one of `draft`, `open`,
`paid`, `uncollectible`, `void`. The `number` column is unique and assigned at
issue time, never at creation time.

answer:
La tabella `user_profiles` [03-data-model.md — user_profiles table].

Contiene `user_id` (uuid, chiave primaria e foreign key verso `users.id`), `display_name`, `avatar_url`, `locale`, `timezone` e `updated_at`. Esiste esattamente una riga di profilo per account, creata in modo lazy alla prima scrittura di profilo [03-data-model.md — user_profiles table].

question: Quale servizio utilizza UserRepository?

context.heading: UserService
context.content:
`UserService` is the entry point for everything about a user account. It
composes the account record and the profile record into the `CurrentUser`
object returned by the API. It depends on `UserRepository` for the account row
and on `ProfileService` for profile fields. `UserService` never queries the
database directly.

context.heading: Layers
context.content:
Requests enter through `AuthController` or `UserController`. Controllers do no
business logic: they validate the request shape and delegate to a service.
Services (`AuthService`, `UserService`, `ProfileService`) hold the business
rules. Repositories (`UserRepository`, `ProfileRepository`, `SessionRepository`)
are the only code allowed to talk to the database.

context.heading: Channel routing
context.content:
`docsync.channels` maps a channel name to a provider bean name, for example
`email: emailDeliveryProvider`. A channel absent from this map is unsupported at
runtime.

context.heading: Request errors
context.content:
`payload_too_large` (HTTP 413) when the payload exceeds
`docsync.render.max-payload-kb`. `unknown_template` (HTTP 404) when
`templateCode` has no active row in `templates`. `unsupported_channel`
(HTTP 400) when `ProviderRouter` has no mapping for the channel.

context.heading: Components at a glance
context.content:
`DocumentRequestController` accepts requests, `RenderService` produces the
artefact, `SignatureService` seals it, `DeliveryService` hands it to a provider
and `DeliveryStatusListener` consumes provider callbacks.

context.heading: AuthService
context.content:
`AuthService` verifies credentials, issues access and refresh tokens and
revokes sessions. It depends on `UserRepository` to load the account and on
`SessionRepository` to persist refresh tokens. Token signing uses the RS256 key
pair loaded at boot from the secret store.

context.heading: Storage
context.content:
Rendered documents are stored in S3 under `documents/{tenantId}/{documentId}.pdf`.
`StorageService` is the only component that touches the S3 client. Object keys
are never reused; a re-render produces a new document id.

answer:
Nella documentazione fornita `UserRepository` è usato da due servizi:

- `UserService`, che se ne serve per la riga di account [02-architecture.md — UserService]
- `AuthService`, che lo usa per caricare l'account durante la verifica delle credenziali [02-architecture.md — AuthService]

I repository sono l'unico codice autorizzato a parlare con il database, quindi i servizi non fanno query dirette [02-architecture.md — Layers].

context.content:

the PDF and enqueues the first payment attempt. Returns HTTP 202. Issuing is
rejected with HTTP 409 `invoice_not_draft` if the invoice is not in `draft`.

answer:

context.heading: StripeGateway
context.content:
`StripeGateway` wraps the Stripe SDK. It exposes `create_payment_intent`,
`capture`, `refund` and `retrieve_event`. It is the single integration point
with Stripe: `PaymentService` calls `StripeGateway`, never the SDK. The gateway
adds the idempotency key and translates Stripe errors into domain errors.

has no mapping in `docsync.channels`. In that case the delivery is recorded with
`unsupported_channel` and no `provider_message_id` is present.

context.heading: Loading
context.content:
Configuration is a pydantic `Settings` object in `billing/config.py`, populated
from environment variables. Unknown variables are ignored; missing required
variables abort startup.

context.heading: users table
context.content:
The `users` table holds the account record: `id` (uuid, primary key), `email`,
`password_hash`, `status`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. The `email` column has a
unique index. `status` is one of `active`, `pending`, `suspended`.

context.heading: Client timeouts
context.content:
Clients are expected to use a timeout larger than the gateway timeout, otherwise
they will give up while the gateway is still waiting for the upstream.

context.heading: user_profiles table
context.content:
The `user_profiles` table holds profile data: `user_id` (uuid, primary key and
foreign key to `users.id`), `display_name`, `avatar_url`, `locale`, `timezone`,
`updated_at`. There is exactly one profile row per account, created lazily on

answer:
Separano account e profilo.

- `users` è il record di account: `id` (uuid, chiave primaria), `email` (indice unico), `password_hash`, `status` (`active`, `pending`, `suspended`), `created_at`, `updated_at` [03-data-model.md — users table].
- `user_profiles` è il record di profilo: `user_id` come chiave primaria e foreign key verso `users.id`, più `display_name`, `avatar_url`, `locale`, `timezone`, `updated_at` [03-data-model.md — user_profiles table].

La relazione è uno a uno, ma la riga di profilo viene creata in modo lazy alla prima scrittura, quindi un account può esistere senza la riga corrispondente in `user_profiles` [03-data-model.md — user_profiles table].

question: Dove viene configurato il timeout delle query al database?

context.heading: Retry settings
context.content:
`PAYMENT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` defaults to 4. `PAYMENT_RETRY_BACKOFF_HOURS` defaults to
`[1, 24, 72]`, so the second attempt happens one hour after the first, the third
a day later and the fourth three days later.

context.heading: Sources
context.content:
Configuration is read at boot by `config/loadConfig.ts`. Values come from
environment variables, with defaults declared in `config/defaults.ts`. There is
no runtime reload: changing configuration requires a restart.

context.heading: RouteResolver
context.content:
`RouteResolver` matches the request path against the route table and produces an
upstream target. The route table is loaded from `routes.yaml` at startup and
refreshed on SIGHUP. An unmatched path returns HTTP 404 `route_not_found`
without contacting any upstream.

context.heading: HTTP settings
context.content:
`HTTP_PORT` defaults to 8080. `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` defaults to 30000 and is
enforced by the server, not by the gateway.

context.heading: Database settings
context.content:
`DATABASE_URL` is the Postgres connection string. `DB_POOL_SIZE` defaults to 10
connections per replica. `DB_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS` defaults to 5000 and is
applied per statement by the pool.

context.heading: Client timeouts
context.content:
Clients are expected to use a timeout larger than the gateway timeout, otherwise
they will give up while the gateway is still waiting for the upstream.

context.heading: Property sources
context.content:
Configuration lives in `application.yaml` and is overridden per environment by
`application-{profile}.yaml` and by environment variables. Spring relaxed
binding applies: `docsync.render.timeout-ms` can be set as
`DOCSYNC_RENDER_TIMEOUT_MS`.

answer:
Con la variabile d'ambiente `DB_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS`, che vale 5000 di default ed è applicata per statement dal pool [06-configuration.md — Database settings].

La configurazione viene letta all'avvio da `config/loadConfig.ts` a partire dalle variabili d'ambiente, con i default dichiarati in `config/defaults.ts`; non esiste reload a runtime, quindi cambiarla richiede un riavvio [06-configuration.md — Sources].

Da non confondere con `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 30000), che è il timeout HTTP del server ed è applicato dal server, non dal gateway [06-configuration.md — HTTP settings].

context.content:

handled by `UserController.getMe`, which calls `UserService.getCurrentUser`.
The response body is:

```json

  "displayName": "Ada Lovelace",

  "locale": "en-GB",
```

`email` and `status` come from the account record.

context.heading: Queue settings
context.content:
`REDIS_URL` is required. `WORKER_CONCURRENCY` defaults to 4.
`JOB_VISIBILITY_TIMEOUT_S` defaults to 300.

context.heading: Charge flow
context.content:
1. `PaymentService.charge` loads the invoice and the previous attempts.
2. `StripeGateway.create_payment_intent` is called with an idempotency key
   derived from `invoice_id` and `attempt_number`.
3. The attempt row is written to `payment_attempts` before the call returns.

2. `authMiddleware` verifies the token and sets `req.auth.userId`.
3. `UserController.getMe` calls `UserService.getCurrentUser(userId)`.

5. `UserService` loads profile fields through `ProfileService.getProfile`.
6. The two records are merged into `CurrentUser` and serialised.

If the profile row is missing, step 5 returns the default profile, so
`displayName` falls back to the email local part.

context.content:
`tls.certPath` and `tls.keyPath` are required in production profiles. `tls.minVersion`
defaults to `1.2`.

mapping lives in `UserRepository.toDomain` and `ProfileRepository.toDomain`.

context.heading: ProfileService
context.content:

does not exist for an account, `ProfileService` returns a default profile built

context.heading: Issuing failures
context.content:
Issuing can fail before any charge: the invoice is not in `draft` state, the
number allocation conflicts (unique violation on `invoices.number`), or the PDF
render step fails and the job is retried by the worker. A failed issue leaves
the invoice in `draft`.

answer:
Percorso documentato del campo:

`GET /me` compone la risposta unendo account e profilo; `displayName` arriva dal record di profilo [04-api-reference.md — GET /me]. Nel flusso, `UserService` carica il profilo tramite `ProfileService.getProfile` e unisce i due record [05-main-flows.md — Current User Flow]. La colonna sorgente è `display_name`, mappata in camelCase da `ProfileRepository.toDomain` [03-data-model.md — Naming].

question: Qual è la durata dell'access token?

context.heading: Request pipeline
context.content:
Each request passes through the pipeline in order: `TLSTerminator`,
`RequestIdMiddleware`, `AuthMiddleware`, `RateLimiter`, `RouteResolver`,
`UpstreamProxy`. A middleware that rejects a request short circuits the rest of
the pipeline.

context.heading: Delivery flow
context.content:
1. Once the request is `rendered`, `DeliveryService.deliver` is invoked.
2. `ProviderRouter` resolves the channel to a provider bean.
3. The provider is called; a `deliveries` row is written with status `queued`
   before the call and updated to `sent` when the provider accepts it.
4. The provider later calls `POST /providers/callbacks/{provider}`.
5. `DeliveryStatusListener` updates the delivery to `accepted`, `rejected` or
   `bounced`.

context.heading: TLS
context.content:
`tls.certPath` and `tls.keyPath` are required in production profiles. `tls.minVersion`
defaults to `1.2`.

context.heading: subscriptions
context.content:
`subscriptions` holds `id`, `user_id`, `plan_code`, `status`, `current_period_start`,
`current_period_end`, `cancel_at_period_end`. `status` is one of `trialing`,
`active`, `past_due`, `canceled`.

context.heading: Token settings
context.content:
`ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL` controls the access token lifetime and defaults to 15
minutes. `REFRESH_TOKEN_TTL` defaults to 30 days. `JWT_KEY_ID` selects which
RS256 key pair is used for signing.

context.heading: Access tokens
context.content:
Access tokens are short lived. The platform standard is a 60 minute access
token lifetime, and Acme Identity follows the platform standard.

answer:
La documentazione fornita contiene informazioni contrastanti su questo punto e non è possibile stabilire quale sia corretta.

- `ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL` controlla la durata dell'access token e vale 15 minuti di default [06-configuration.md — Token settings].
- La durata standard di piattaforma per l'access token è indicata in 60 minuti, e il servizio dichiara di seguire lo standard di piattaforma [08-token-lifetimes.md — Access tokens].

Le due fonti non sono conciliabili con le informazioni disponibili: servirebbe verificare il valore effettivo di `ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL` nell'ambiente o quale delle due pagine è più recente.

2. `authMiddleware` verifies the token and sets `req.auth.userId`.
3. `UserController.getMe` calls `UserService.getCurrentUser(userId)`.
4. `UserService` loads the account through `UserRepository.findById`.
5. `UserService` loads profile fields through `ProfileService.getProfile`.
6. The two records are merged into `CurrentUser` and serialised.

context.content:
`ProfileService` owns profile fields: `displayName`, `avatarUrl`, `locale` and
`timezone`. It reads and writes through `ProfileRepository`. When a profile row
does not exist for an account, `ProfileService` returns a default profile built
from the account email local part.

`DeliveryProvider` interface. Implementations are `EmailDeliveryProvider`,
`PecDeliveryProvider` and `PortalDeliveryProvider`. Selection is driven by the

`updated_at`. There is exactly one profile row per account, created lazily on

context.content:
Creates a draft invoice for a subscription. Body: `{ subscriptionId, lines }`.
Returns HTTP 201 with the invoice in `draft` status. Creating an invoice does
not charge anything.

Non è un errore: il profilo viene sostituito da un default.

question: Which HTTP status is returned when the caller lacks the required scope?

context.heading: RenderService
context.content:
`RenderService` resolves the template by `templateCode`, merges the payload and
produces a PDF through the `PdfRenderer` component. Rendering is synchronous and
bounded: a render that exceeds the render timeout is aborted and the request is
marked `render_failed`.

context.heading: GET /users/:id
context.content:
Internal route, requires the `users:read` scope. Returns the same shape as
`GET /me` for an arbitrary account id. Used by other services.

context.heading: Storage
context.content:
Rendered documents are stored in S3 under `documents/{tenantId}/{documentId}.pdf`.
`StorageService` is the only component that touches the S3 client. Object keys
are never reused; a re-render produces a new document id.

context.heading: Document production flow
context.content:
1. `POST /documents` stores a `document_requests` row with status `received`.
2. The request is queued; a worker moves it to `rendering`.
3. `RenderService` resolves the active template and renders the PDF.
4. `SignatureService` seals the PDF.
5. `StorageService` uploads it and writes the `documents` row.
6. The request moves to `rendered`.

context.heading: Authorisation errors
context.content:
`insufficient_scope` (HTTP 403) is returned when a route requires a scope the
token does not carry, for example calling `GET /users/:id` without
`users:read`.

context.heading: RouteResolver
context.content:
`RouteResolver` matches the request path against the route table and produces an
upstream target. The route table is loaded from `routes.yaml` at startup and
refreshed on SIGHUP. An unmatched path returns HTTP 404 `route_not_found`
without contacting any upstream.

HTTP 403 with the error code `insufficient_scope` [07-errors.md — Authorisation errors].

The documented example is calling `GET /users/:id` without the `users:read` scope, which is the scope that route requires [07-errors.md — Authorisation errors] [04-api-reference.md — GET /users/:id].

question: Qual è la differenza tra GET /me e GET /users/:id?

context.heading: Components
context.content:
`InvoiceService` builds invoices from subscription and usage records.
`PaymentService` executes charges and refunds. `StripeGateway` is the only
component that performs HTTP calls to Stripe. `WebhookHandler` consumes Stripe
callbacks. `SubscriptionRepository`, `InvoiceRepository` and `PaymentRepository`
own database access.

context.heading: Purpose
context.content:
Mesh Gateway is the single ingress for every public API call at Acme. It is a Go
service that terminates TLS, authenticates the caller, applies rate limits and
forwards the request to the right upstream service. It holds no business logic
and no database.

context.heading: GET /me
context.content:
Returns the authenticated user. The route requires a valid bearer token and is
handled by `UserController.getMe`, which calls `UserService.getCurrentUser`.
The response body is:

```json
{
  "id": "uuid",
  "email": "user@example.com",
  "displayName": "Ada Lovelace",
  "avatarUrl": "https://cdn.acme.dev/avatars/ada.png",
  "locale": "en-GB",
  "status": "active"
}
```

`displayName`, `avatarUrl` and `locale` come from the profile record. `id`,
`email` and `status` come from the account record.

context.heading: GET /users/:id
context.content:
Internal route, requires the `users:read` scope. Returns the same shape as
`GET /me` for an arbitrary account id. Used by other services.

context.heading: Property sources
context.content:
Configuration lives in `application.yaml` and is overridden per environment by
`application-{profile}.yaml` and by environment variables. Spring relaxed
binding applies: `docsync.render.timeout-ms` can be set as
`DOCSYNC_RENDER_TIMEOUT_MS`.

context.heading: Issuing failures
context.content:
Issuing can fail before any charge: the invoice is not in `draft` state, the
number allocation conflicts (unique violation on `invoices.number`), or the PDF
render step fails and the job is retried by the worker. A failed issue leaves
the invoice in `draft`.

Stessa forma di risposta, destinatari diversi.

- `GET /me` restituisce l'utente autenticato e richiede soltanto un bearer token valido [04-api-reference.md — GET /me].
- `GET /users/:id` è una rotta interna, richiede lo scope `users:read` e restituisce la stessa forma di `GET /me` per un id account arbitrario; è usata dagli altri servizi [04-api-reference.md — GET /users/:id].

question: Il servizio mantiene sessioni in memoria?

context.heading: Default upstream timeout
context.content:
The platform timeout policy sets the default upstream timeout to 10000 ms. Mesh
Gateway applies this default to every route that does not declare its own
`timeoutMs`.

context.heading: Runtime
context.content:
The service runs as a stateless container. Two replicas are deployed per
environment. Sessions are not held in memory: every request is authenticated
from the bearer token, so any replica can serve any request.

context.heading: sessions table
context.content:
The `sessions` table holds refresh tokens: `id`, `user_id`, `refresh_token_hash`,
`user_agent`, `expires_at`, `revoked_at`. Access tokens are never stored; only
refresh tokens are persisted, and only as a hash.

context.heading: GET /documents/{id}
context.content:
Returns the document request with its current status and, once rendered, the
document id and a short-lived download URL.

context.heading: Rate limiting
context.content:
`rateLimit.defaultRps` is 50 requests per second per caller.
`rateLimit.burst` is 100. `rateLimit.redisUrl` is required; without it the

context.heading: templates
context.content:
`templates` holds `code` (primary key), `version`, `engine`, `body`,
`active`. Only rows with `active = true` can be resolved by `RenderService`.

answer:
No. Il servizio gira come container stateless e le sessioni non sono tenute in memoria: ogni richiesta viene autenticata a partire dal bearer token, quindi qualsiasi replica può servire qualsiasi richiesta [01-overview.md — Runtime].

question: Quale servizio comunica con Stripe?

context.heading: deliveries
context.content:
`deliveries` holds `id`, `document_id`, `provider`, `recipient`, `status`,
`provider_message_id`, `error_code`, `attempt_number`, `created_at`,
`updated_at`. `status` is one of `queued`, `sent`, `accepted`, `rejected`,
`bounced`.

context.heading: AuthService
context.content:
`AuthService` verifies credentials, issues access and refresh tokens and
revokes sessions. It depends on `UserRepository` to load the account and on
`SessionRepository` to persist refresh tokens. Token signing uses the RS256 key
pair loaded at boot from the secret store.

context.content:
`validation_failed` (HTTP 422) is returned when the request body does not match
the expected shape. The `message` field lists the offending fields.

context.content:
`PaymentService` decides when to charge, how many times to retry and when to
mark an invoice as uncollectible. It depends on `StripeGateway` for the actual
call and on `PaymentRepository` to record each attempt. Retry state lives in the
`payment_attempts` table, not in memory.

context.heading: Position in the platform
context.content:
Clients talk only to the gateway. Internal services are not reachable from
outside the cluster. The gateway adds the `X-Request-Id` and `X-Caller-Id`
headers that downstream services log and propagate.

context.heading: StripeGateway
context.content:
`StripeGateway` wraps the Stripe SDK. It exposes `create_payment_intent`,

with Stripe: `PaymentService` calls `StripeGateway`, never the SDK. The gateway

context.content:

It is a Python 3.11 FastAPI service. It is the only service allowed to talk to
the payment provider; every other service asks Billing Core instead of calling
the provider directly.

`PaymentService` non usa mai l'SDK direttamente: passa sempre da `StripeGateway` [02-architecture.md — StripeGateway] [02-architecture.md — PaymentService].

question: In quali casi l'emissione di una fattura può fallire?

context.heading: Files and env
context.content:

Environment variables prefixed with `GW_` override any key, for example
`GW_UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_MS`.

context.heading: AuthService

context.heading: Invoice issuing flow
context.content:
1. `POST /invoices/{id}/issue` reaches `InvoiceService.issue`.
2. The invoice status is checked; only `draft` can be issued.
3. `InvoiceRepository.assign_number` allocates the next invoice number.
4. The PDF is rendered and uploaded; `pdf_url` is stored.
5. A `charge_invoice` job is pushed to the queue.
6. `billing-worker` picks up the job and calls `PaymentService.charge`.

context.heading: Delivery errors
context.content:
Provider errors are normalised to `provider_rejected`, `provider_unavailable`
and `recipient_invalid`. `recipient_invalid` is final. `provider_unavailable` is
retryable. `provider_rejected` is retryable only when the provider marks the
error code as retryable.

context.heading: Issuing failures
context.content:
Issuing can fail before any charge: the invoice is not in `draft` state, the
number allocation conflicts (unique violation on `invoices.number`), or the PDF
render step fails and the job is retried by the worker. A failed issue leaves
the invoice in `draft`.

context.heading: POST /invoices/{id}/issue
context.content:
Moves an invoice from `draft` to `open`, assigns the invoice `number`, renders
the PDF and enqueues the first payment attempt. Returns HTTP 202. Issuing is
rejected with HTTP 409 `invoice_not_draft` if the invoice is not in `draft`.

context.heading: SignatureService
context.content:
`SignatureService` applies a PAdES seal using the certificate loaded from the
HSM at startup. If the certificate cannot be loaded the application refuses to
start. Signing happens after rendering and before storage.

answer:
Secondo la documentazione fornita l'emissione può fallire prima di qualsiasi addebito, in tre modi:

1. La fattura non è in stato `draft`: la rotta risponde HTTP 409 `invoice_not_draft` [04-api-reference.md — POST /invoices/{id}/issue] [07-errors.md — Issuing failures].
2. L'allocazione del numero va in conflitto, per violazione dell'indice unico su `invoices.number` [07-errors.md — Issuing failures].
3. Il render del PDF fallisce e il job viene ritentato dal worker [07-errors.md — Issuing failures].

In tutti i casi un'emissione fallita lascia la fattura in `draft` [07-errors.md — Issuing failures]. Il passaggio di stato e l'assegnazione del numero avvengono in `InvoiceService.issue`, prima che venga messo in coda il job `charge_invoice` [05-main-flows.md — Invoice issuing flow].

context.heading: Upstream errors
context.content:
`upstream_timeout` (HTTP 504) when the upstream exceeds the route timeout.
`upstream_unavailable` (HTTP 502) when the connection fails. The gateway never
converts an upstream 5xx into a 2xx: upstream status codes above 499 are passed
through unchanged, with the body replaced by the gateway error envelope.

mark an invoice as uncollectible. It depends on `StripeGateway` for the actual
call and on `PaymentRepository` to record each attempt. Retry state lives in the

HSM at startup. If the certificate cannot be loaded the application refuses to
start. Signing happens after rendering and before storage.

context.heading: Health

readiness probe and additionally checks the Redis connection used by
`RateLimiter`.

answer:
Nella tabella `payment_attempts`: una riga per ogni tentativo di addebito, con `id`, `invoice_id`, `provider_intent_id`, `status`, `error_code`, `attempt_number`, `created_at`. Il numero di retry corrente di una fattura è il numero di righe per quella fattura [03-data-model.md — payment_attempts].

question: Dove viene configurato il timeout verso Stripe?

context.heading: POST /auth/refresh
context.content:
Accepts `{ refreshToken }` and returns a new access token. If the refresh token
is unknown, expired or already revoked, the route returns HTTP 401 with
`{ "error": "invalid_refresh_token" }`.

context.heading: Request errors
context.content:
`payload_too_large` (HTTP 413) when the payload exceeds
`docsync.render.max-payload-kb`. `unknown_template` (HTTP 404) when
`templateCode` has no active row in `templates`. `unsupported_channel`
(HTTP 400) when `ProviderRouter` has no mapping for the channel.

context.heading: Purpose
context.content:
Mesh Gateway is the single ingress for every public API call at Acme. It is a Go
service that terminates TLS, authenticates the caller, applies rate limits and
forwards the request to the right upstream service. It holds no business logic
and no database.

context.heading: Provider settings
context.content:

defaults to 8000 and is passed to the Stripe SDK by `StripeGateway`.

2. `AuthService.authenticate` loads the account by email via `UserRepository`.
3. The password is verified against `password_hash` with argon2id.
4. On success `AuthService` issues an access token and a refresh token, and

question: Come viene garantita l'idempotenza dei webhook?

context.heading: Webhook flow
context.content:
1. Stripe posts to `POST /webhooks/stripe`.
2. `WebhookHandler.receive` verifies the signature and inserts into
   `webhook_events`; a duplicate `provider_event_id` is ignored.
3. A `process_event` job is queued.
4. `billing-worker` maps `payment_intent.succeeded` to invoice `paid` and
   `payment_intent.payment_failed` to a new retry decision.

context.heading: Webhook failures
context.content:
A webhook with an invalid signature is rejected with HTTP 400
`invalid_signature` and is not stored. A webhook whose `provider_event_id` is
already present is acknowledged with HTTP 200 and dropped.

context.heading: Billing routes
context.content:
`/v1/invoices/*` and `/v1/subscriptions/*` forward to the `billing-core`
upstream and require the caller to carry a billing scope.

context.heading: POST /auth/login
context.content:
Accepts `{ email, password }`. On success returns `{ accessToken, refreshToken,
expiresIn }` with HTTP 200. On invalid credentials returns HTTP 401 with body
`{ "error": "invalid_credentials" }`. The route is rate limited to 10 attempts
per email per 15 minutes.

context.heading: Error envelope
context.content:
Every error response uses `{ "error": "<code>", "message": "<human text>" }`.
The `error` code is stable and safe to switch on; `message` is not.

context.heading: webhook_events
context.content:
`webhook_events` stores every received Stripe event with `provider_event_id`
(unique), `type`, `payload`, `processed_at`. The unique index on
`provider_event_id` is what makes webhook processing idempotent.

context.heading: Refresh tokens
context.content:
Refresh tokens live for 30 days and are rotated on every use: the previous
refresh token is revoked as soon as a new one is issued.

answer:
Tramite l'indice unico su `provider_event_id` nella tabella `webhook_events`.

- Ogni evento Stripe ricevuto viene salvato in `webhook_events` con `provider_event_id` unico, `type`, `payload`, `processed_at`; è proprio quell'indice unico a rendere idempotente l'elaborazione [03-data-model.md — webhook_events].
- `WebhookHandler.receive` verifica la firma e inserisce l'evento; un `provider_event_id` duplicato viene ignorato [05-main-flows.md — Webhook flow].
- Un webhook già presente viene comunque confermato con HTTP 200 e scartato [07-errors.md — Webhook failures].

question: POST /invoices/{id}/issue restituisce 409. Cosa dovrei controllare?

context.heading: invoices
context.content:
`invoices` holds `id`, `subscription_id`, `number`, `currency`, `amount_cents`,
`status`, `issued_at`, `due_at`, `pdf_url`. `status` is one of `draft`, `open`,
`paid`, `uncollectible`, `void`. The `number` column is unique and assigned at
issue time, never at creation time.

context.heading: UserService
context.content:
`UserService` is the entry point for everything about a user account. It
composes the account record and the profile record into the `CurrentUser`
object returned by the API. It depends on `UserRepository` for the account row
and on `ProfileService` for profile fields. `UserService` never queries the
database directly.

context.heading: UpstreamProxy
context.content:
`UpstreamProxy` performs the forwarded call. It applies the per-route timeout,
retries idempotent methods and records the upstream latency metric
`gateway_upstream_duration_seconds`.

context.heading: routes.yaml
context.content:
Each entry declares `path`, `methods`, `upstream`, `timeoutMs`, `authRequired`
and `rateLimit`. The first matching entry wins, so more specific paths must be
declared before wildcards.

context.heading: Error envelope
context.content:
Every error response uses `{ "error": "<code>", "message": "<human text>" }`.
The `error` code is stable and safe to switch on; `message` is not.

context.heading: POST /invoices/{id}/issue
context.content:
Moves an invoice from `draft` to `open`, assigns the invoice `number`, renders
the PDF and enqueues the first payment attempt. Returns HTTP 202. Issuing is
rejected with HTTP 409 `invoice_not_draft` if the invoice is not in `draft`.

context.heading: Domain errors
context.content:
`invoice_not_draft` (HTTP 409) when issuing a non-draft invoice.
`invoice_not_payable` (HTTP 409) when charging an invoice that is not `open`.
`refund_exceeds_amount` (HTTP 422) when the refund amount is larger than the
paid amount.

answer:
Il 409 documentato per questa rotta è uno solo: `invoice_not_draft`, restituito quando la fattura non è in stato `draft` [04-api-reference.md — POST /invoices/{id}/issue] [07-errors.md — Domain errors].

Verifiche che derivano dalla documentazione:
1. Controllare lo stato corrente della fattura: i valori possibili sono `draft`, `open`, `paid`, `uncollectible`, `void`, e solo `draft` può essere emessa [03-data-model.md — invoices] [04-api-reference.md — POST /invoices/{id}/issue].
2. Verificare se l'emissione era già stata eseguita: l'emissione porta la fattura a `open`, quindi una seconda chiamata sulla stessa fattura ricadrebbe nello stesso 409 [04-api-reference.md — POST /invoices/{id}/issue].

Nota: `invoice_not_payable` è anch'esso HTTP 409, ma la documentazione lo associa all'addebito di una fattura non `open`, non a questa rotta [07-errors.md — Domain errors].

question: Quali errori del provider fanno scattare un retry?

context.heading: Retry settings
context.content:
`PAYMENT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` defaults to 4. `PAYMENT_RETRY_BACKOFF_HOURS` defaults to
`[1, 24, 72]`, so the second attempt happens one hour after the first, the third
a day later and the fourth three days later.

context.heading: GET /users/:id
context.content:
Internal route, requires the `users:read` scope. Returns the same shape as
`GET /me` for an arbitrary account id. Used by other services.

context.heading: TLS
context.content:
`tls.certPath` and `tls.keyPath` are required in production profiles. `tls.minVersion`
defaults to `1.2`.

context.heading: Position in the platform
context.content:
Clients talk only to the gateway. Internal services are not reachable from
outside the cluster. The gateway adds the `X-Request-Id` and `X-Caller-Id`
headers that downstream services log and propagate.

context.heading: GET /me
context.content:
Returns the authenticated user. The route requires a valid bearer token and is
handled by `UserController.getMe`, which calls `UserService.getCurrentUser`.
The response body is:

```json
{
  "id": "uuid",
  "email": "user@example.com",
  "displayName": "Ada Lovelace",
  "avatarUrl": "https://cdn.acme.dev/avatars/ada.png",
  "locale": "en-GB",
  "status": "active"
}
```

`displayName`, `avatarUrl` and `locale` come from the profile record. `id`,
`email` and `status` come from the account record.

context.heading: Provider errors
context.content:
`StripeGateway` translates provider failures into `ProviderCardError`,
`ProviderRateLimited` and `ProviderUnavailable`. `ProviderCardError` is final:
the attempt is recorded and no retry is scheduled. `ProviderRateLimited` and
`ProviderUnavailable` are retryable and consume one of the
`PAYMENT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` attempts.

answer:
Sono retryable `ProviderRateLimited` e `ProviderUnavailable`, e ciascun tentativo consuma uno dei `PAYMENT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` [07-errors.md — Provider errors].

`ProviderCardError` invece è definitivo: il tentativo viene registrato e non viene pianificato nessun retry [07-errors.md — Provider errors].

I parametri sono `PAYMENT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (default 4) e `PAYMENT_RETRY_BACKOFF_HOURS` (default `[1, 24, 72]`), quindi il secondo tentativo avviene un'ora dopo il primo, il terzo un giorno dopo e il quarto tre giorni dopo [06-configuration.md — Retry settings].

question: Perché ogni consumer della coda deve essere idempotente?

context.heading: Current User Flow
context.content:
1. The client calls `GET /me` with a bearer token.
2. `authMiddleware` verifies the token and sets `req.auth.userId`.
3. `UserController.getMe` calls `UserService.getCurrentUser(userId)`.
4. `UserService` loads the account through `UserRepository.findById`.
5. `UserService` loads profile fields through `ProfileService.getProfile`.
6. The two records are merged into `CurrentUser` and serialised.

If the profile row is missing, step 5 returns the default profile, so
`displayName` falls back to the email local part.

context.heading: Queue
context.content:
Long running work is pushed to Redis and consumed by `billing-worker`. Invoice
issuing, dunning emails and webhook replays are queued. The queue is at-least
once: every consumer must be idempotent.

context.heading: Channel routing
context.content:
`docsync.channels` maps a channel name to a provider bean name, for example
`email: emailDeliveryProvider`. A channel absent from this map is unsupported at
runtime.

context.heading: Authentication flow
context.content:
Every protected route passes through `authMiddleware`. The middleware reads the
`Authorization: Bearer <token>` header, verifies the RS256 signature, checks the
`exp` claim and loads the account id from the `sub` claim. It then attaches
`req.auth = { userId, scopes }`. Routes never parse the token themselves.

context.heading: DeliveryService
context.content:
`DeliveryService` selects a provider for each delivery and calls it through the
`DeliveryProvider` interface. Implementations are `EmailDeliveryProvider`,
`PecDeliveryProvider` and `PortalDeliveryProvider`. Selection is driven by the
`channel` field of the request, resolved by `ProviderRouter`.

context.heading: Deployment
context.content:
The service runs as two workloads from the same image: the HTTP API and the
`billing-worker` process that drains the job queue. Both are deployed together
and share the same configuration.

answer:
Perché la coda è at-least once: ogni consumer deve essere idempotente [02-architecture.md — Queue].

Il lavoro lungo viene spinto su Redis e consumato da `billing-worker`; in coda finiscono l'emissione delle fatture, le email di dunning e i replay dei webhook [02-architecture.md — Queue]. `billing-worker` è uno dei due workload avviati dalla stessa immagine, insieme all'API HTTP, e condivide la stessa configurazione [01-overview.md — Deployment].

question: Cosa succede dalla chiamata a issue fino alla fattura pagata?

context.heading: Charge flow
context.content:
1. `PaymentService.charge` loads the invoice and the previous attempts.
2. `StripeGateway.create_payment_intent` is called with an idempotency key
   derived from `invoice_id` and `attempt_number`.
3. The attempt row is written to `payment_attempts` before the call returns.
4. Stripe confirms asynchronously; the outcome arrives via webhook.

context.heading: Property sources
context.content:
Configuration lives in `application.yaml` and is overridden per environment by
`application-{profile}.yaml` and by environment variables. Spring relaxed
binding applies: `docsync.render.timeout-ms` can be set as
`DOCSYNC_RENDER_TIMEOUT_MS`.

context.heading: Invoice issuing flow
context.content:
1. `POST /invoices/{id}/issue` reaches `InvoiceService.issue`.
2. The invoice status is checked; only `draft` can be issued.
3. `InvoiceRepository.assign_number` allocates the next invoice number.
4. The PDF is rendered and uploaded; `pdf_url` is stored.
5. A `charge_invoice` job is pushed to the queue.
6. `billing-worker` picks up the job and calls `PaymentService.charge`.

context.heading: Webhook flow
context.content:
1. Stripe posts to `POST /webhooks/stripe`.
2. `WebhookHandler.receive` verifies the signature and inserts into
   `webhook_events`; a duplicate `provider_event_id` is ignored.
3. A `process_event` job is queued.
4. `billing-worker` maps `payment_intent.succeeded` to invoice `paid` and
   `payment_intent.payment_failed` to a new retry decision.

context.heading: ProviderRouter
context.content:
`ProviderRouter` maps a channel to a provider bean. If the channel has no
mapping the delivery is rejected immediately with `unsupported_channel` and no
provider is called. The routing table is built at startup from configuration.

context.heading: Purpose
context.content:
DocSync generates, signs and delivers documents (contracts, certificates,
policy files) to end users. It is a Java 21 Spring Boot service. Documents are
produced from templates, stored in object storage and delivered through one of
several delivery providers.

context.heading: Token settings
context.content:
`ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL` controls the access token lifetime and defaults to 15
minutes. `REFRESH_TOKEN_TTL` defaults to 30 days. `JWT_KEY_ID` selects which
RS256 key pair is used for signing.

answer:
Il percorso documentato attraversa tre flussi.

1. Emissione: `POST /invoices/{id}/issue` chiama `InvoiceService.issue`, che verifica lo stato `draft`, alloca il numero con `InvoiceRepository.assign_number`, renderizza e carica il PDF salvando `pdf_url`, e mette in coda il job `charge_invoice` [05-main-flows.md — Invoice issuing flow].
2. Addebito: `billing-worker` prende il job e chiama `PaymentService.charge`, che carica fattura e tentativi precedenti, chiama `StripeGateway.create_payment_intent` con una idempotency key derivata da `invoice_id` e `attempt_number`, e scrive la riga in `payment_attempts` prima che la chiamata ritorni [05-main-flows.md — Invoice issuing flow] [05-main-flows.md — Charge flow].
3. Conferma: Stripe conferma in modo asincrono; l'evento arriva su `POST /webhooks/stripe`, viene inserito in `webhook_events` e messo in coda come `process_event`. Il worker mappa `payment_intent.succeeded` sullo stato `paid` della fattura e `payment_intent.payment_failed` su una nuova decisione di retry [05-main-flows.md — Charge flow] [05-main-flows.md — Webhook flow].

question: Which components are allowed to access the database?

context.heading: Gateway errors
context.content:
`route_not_found` (HTTP 404) when no route matches. `unauthenticated` (HTTP 401)
when the bearer token is missing or invalid. `forbidden_scope` (HTTP 403) when
the route requires a scope the caller does not have. `rate_limited` (HTTP 429)
when the token bucket is empty.

context.content:

2. `ProfileService.updateProfile` writes the changed fields through
   `ProfileRepository.upsert`, creating the row if it does not exist.
3. `UserService.getCurrentUser` is called again to build the response.

`PaymentService` executes charges and refunds. `StripeGateway` is the only
component that performs HTTP calls to Stripe. `WebhookHandler` consumes Stripe
callbacks. `SubscriptionRepository`, `InvoiceRepository` and `PaymentRepository`
own database access.

context.content:
`RouteResolver` matches the request path against the route table and produces an
upstream target. The route table is loaded from `routes.yaml` at startup and

minutes. `REFRESH_TOKEN_TTL` defaults to 30 days. `JWT_KEY_ID` selects which

The other listed components have different roles: `InvoiceService` builds invoices, `PaymentService` executes charges and refunds, `StripeGateway` performs the Stripe HTTP calls and `WebhookHandler` consumes Stripe callbacks [02-architecture.md — Components].

question: Come vengono gestiti i rimborsi parziali e quanto tempo impiegano ad arrivare al cliente?

context.heading: POST /invoices/{id}/refund
context.content:
Refunds a paid invoice through `PaymentService.refund`. Partial refunds are
accepted via an optional `amountCents`. Returns HTTP 200 with the refund record.

context.heading: POST /documents
context.content:

Returns HTTP 202 with `{ requestId, status: "received" }`. The work continues

context.content:

question: Cosa succede se la firma di un webhook non è valida?

context.heading: Client timeouts
context.content:
Clients are expected to use a timeout larger than the gateway timeout, otherwise
they will give up while the gateway is still waiting for the upstream.

context.heading: POST /webhooks/stripe
context.content:
Receives Stripe callbacks. The route verifies the Stripe signature header
before doing anything else, stores the raw event in `webhook_events` and returns
HTTP 200 immediately. Processing happens asynchronously in `billing-worker`.

context.heading: Webhook failures
context.content:
A webhook with an invalid signature is rejected with HTTP 400
`invalid_signature` and is not stored. A webhook whose `provider_event_id` is
already present is acknowledged with HTTP 200 and dropped.

context.heading: Error envelope
context.content:
`{ "error": "<code>", "requestId": "<id>" }`. The `requestId` matches the
`X-Request-Id` header and is the key to correlate gateway and upstream logs.

context.heading: Components at a glance
context.content:
`DocumentRequestController` accepts requests, `RenderService` produces the
artefact, `SignatureService` seals it, `DeliveryService` hands it to a provider
and `DeliveryStatusListener` consumes provider callbacks.

context.heading: GET /users/:id
context.content:
Internal route, requires the `users:read` scope. Returns the same shape as
`GET /me` for an arbitrary account id. Used by other services.

answer:
Il webhook viene rifiutato con HTTP 400 `invalid_signature` e non viene salvato [07-errors.md — Webhook failures].

La verifica della firma è la prima cosa che fa la rotta, prima di qualsiasi altra operazione; solo dopo l'evento grezzo viene salvato in `webhook_events` e la rotta risponde subito HTTP 200, lasciando l'elaborazione a `billing-worker` [04-api-reference.md — POST /webhooks/stripe].

question: L'utente non riceve il documento. Da dove parto?

context.heading: The recipient did not receive the document
context.content:

question: Il provider non viene mai chiamato. Perché?

context.heading: Purpose
context.content:
Acme Identity is the internal service that owns user accounts, profiles and
session tokens for every Acme product. It is a TypeScript service running on
Node 20 and exposes a REST API behind the internal gateway. All other services
treat it as the single source of truth for "who is this user".

context.heading: ProviderRouter
context.content:
`ProviderRouter` maps a channel to a provider bean. If the channel has no
mapping the delivery is rejected immediately with `unsupported_channel` and no
provider is called. The routing table is built at startup from configuration.

context.heading: Webhook flow
context.content:
1. Stripe posts to `POST /webhooks/stripe`.
2. `WebhookHandler.receive` verifies the signature and inserts into
   `webhook_events`; a duplicate `provider_event_id` is ignored.
3. A `process_event` job is queued.
4. `billing-worker` maps `payment_intent.succeeded` to invoice `paid` and
   `payment_intent.payment_failed` to a new retry decision.

context.heading: A provider was never called
context.content:
`ProviderRouter` rejects a delivery before calling any provider when the channel
has no mapping in `docsync.channels`. In that case the delivery is recorded with
`unsupported_channel` and no `provider_message_id` is present.

context.heading: Channel routing
context.content:
`docsync.channels` maps a channel name to a provider bean name, for example
`email: emailDeliveryProvider`. A channel absent from this map is unsupported at
runtime.

context.heading: GET /users/:id
context.content:
Internal route, requires the `users:read` scope. Returns the same shape as
`GET /me` for an arbitrary account id. Used by other services.

context.heading: Refresh tokens
context.content:
Refresh tokens live for 30 days and are rotated on every use: the previous
refresh token is revoked as soon as a new one is issued.

answer:
La causa documentata è il routing del canale.

`ProviderRouter` rifiuta la delivery prima di chiamare qualsiasi provider quando il canale non ha una mappatura in `docsync.channels`; in quel caso la delivery viene registrata con `unsupported_channel` e non è presente nessun `provider_message_id` [08-troubleshooting.md — A provider was never called].

Coerentemente, se il canale non ha mappatura la delivery viene rifiutata subito con `unsupported_channel` e nessun provider viene chiamato [02-architecture.md — ProviderRouter]. La mappatura è `docsync.channels`, che associa un nome di canale a un bean provider, ad esempio `email: emailDeliveryProvider`; un canale assente dalla mappa è non supportato a runtime [06-configuration.md — Channel routing].

Da verificare: il valore del campo `channel` della richiesta e la presenza della chiave corrispondente in `docsync.channels`. La tabella di routing è costruita all'avvio dalla configurazione, quindi una modifica non applicata a runtime è un'ipotesi coerente ma non confermata dalle sezioni fornite [02-architecture.md — ProviderRouter].

question: Qual è il ruolo di DeliveryService?

context.heading: Kubernetes
context.content:
The gateway is deployed as a Deployment with 4 replicas and a HorizontalPodAutoscaler
targeting 60% CPU. The Service is of type LoadBalancer. Config is mounted from
the `mesh-gateway-config` ConfigMap; `routes.yaml` lives in the same ConfigMap.

context.heading: Validation errors
context.content:
`validation_failed` (HTTP 422) is returned when the request body does not match
the expected shape. The `message` field lists the offending fields.

context.heading: DeliveryService
context.content:
`DeliveryService` selects a provider for each delivery and calls it through the
`DeliveryProvider` interface. Implementations are `EmailDeliveryProvider`,
`PecDeliveryProvider` and `PortalDeliveryProvider`. Selection is driven by the
`channel` field of the request, resolved by `ProviderRouter`.

context.heading: ProviderRouter
context.content:
`ProviderRouter` maps a channel to a provider bean. If the channel has no
mapping the delivery is rejected immediately with `unsupported_channel` and no
provider is called. The routing table is built at startup from configuration.

context.content:
1. `PaymentService.charge` loads the invoice and the previous attempts.
2. `StripeGateway.create_payment_intent` is called with an idempotency key
   derived from `invoice_id` and `attempt_number`.
3. The attempt row is written to `payment_attempts` before the call returns.
4. Stripe confirms asynchronously; the outcome arrives via webhook.

context.content:

`DeliveryService` sceglie un provider per ogni delivery e lo chiama attraverso l'interfaccia `DeliveryProvider` [02-architecture.md — DeliveryService].

Le implementazioni documentate sono `EmailDeliveryProvider`, `PecDeliveryProvider` e `PortalDeliveryProvider`, e la selezione è guidata dal campo `channel` della richiesta, risolto da `ProviderRouter` [02-architecture.md — DeliveryService]. `ProviderRouter` costruisce la tabella di routing all'avvio dalla configurazione [02-architecture.md — ProviderRouter].

question: Quali errori di rendering sono previsti e vengono ritentati?

context.heading: RenderService
context.content:
`RenderService` resolves the template by `templateCode`, merges the payload and
produces a PDF through the `PdfRenderer` component. Rendering is synchronous and
bounded: a render that exceeds the render timeout is aborted and the request is
marked `render_failed`.

context.heading: Charge flow
context.content:
1. `PaymentService.charge` loads the invoice and the previous attempts.
2. `StripeGateway.create_payment_intent` is called with an idempotency key
   derived from `invoice_id` and `attempt_number`.
3. The attempt row is written to `payment_attempts` before the call returns.
4. Stripe confirms asynchronously; the outcome arrives via webhook.

context.heading: Queue
context.content:
Long running work is pushed to Redis and consumed by `billing-worker`. Invoice
issuing, dunning emails and webhook replays are queued. The queue is at-least
once: every consumer must be idempotent.

context.heading: Render errors
context.content:
`render_timeout` when the render exceeds `docsync.render.timeout-ms`.
`template_render_error` when the template engine throws. Both move the request
to `render_failed`; neither is retried automatically.

context.heading: UpstreamProxy
context.content:
`UpstreamProxy` performs the forwarded call. It applies the per-route timeout,
retries idempotent methods and records the upstream latency metric
`gateway_upstream_duration_seconds`.

context.heading: Position in the platform
context.content:
Clients talk only to the gateway. Internal services are not reachable from
outside the cluster. The gateway adds the `X-Request-Id` and `X-Caller-Id`
headers that downstream services log and propagate.

answer:
Sono documentati due errori di render e nessuno dei due viene ritentato automaticamente.

- `render_timeout`, quando il render supera `docsync.render.timeout-ms` [07-errors.md — Render errors].
- `template_render_error`, quando il motore di template solleva un errore [07-errors.md — Render errors].

Entrambi portano la richiesta in `render_failed` e nessuno dei due è ritentato automaticamente [07-errors.md — Render errors]. Questo è coerente con `RenderService`, che è sincrono e limitato: un render oltre il timeout viene interrotto e la richiesta marcata `render_failed` [02-architecture.md — RenderService].

question: Dove finisce il PDF dopo essere stato generato?

context.heading: Storage
context.content:
Rendered documents are stored in S3 under `documents/{tenantId}/{documentId}.pdf`.
`StorageService` is the only component that touches the S3 client. Object keys
are never reused; a re-render produces a new document id.

context.heading: documents
context.content:
`documents` holds `id`, `request_id`, `storage_key`, `checksum_sha256`,
`signed`, `size_bytes`, `created_at`. One row per successfully rendered
artefact.

context.heading: Webhook failures
context.content:
A webhook with an invalid signature is rejected with HTTP 400
`invalid_signature` and is not stored. A webhook whose `provider_event_id` is
already present is acknowledged with HTTP 200 and dropped.

context.heading: users table
context.content:
The `users` table holds the account record: `id` (uuid, primary key), `email`,
`password_hash`, `status`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. The `email` column has a
unique index. `status` is one of `active`, `pending`, `suspended`.

context.heading: Current User Flow
context.content:
1. The client calls `GET /me` with a bearer token.
2. `authMiddleware` verifies the token and sets `req.auth.userId`.
3. `UserController.getMe` calls `UserService.getCurrentUser(userId)`.
4. `UserService` loads the account through `UserRepository.findById`.
5. `UserService` loads profile fields through `ProfileService.getProfile`.
6. The two records are merged into `CurrentUser` and serialised.

If the profile row is missing, step 5 returns the default profile, so
`displayName` falls back to the email local part.

context.heading: Document production flow
context.content:
1. `POST /documents` stores a `document_requests` row with status `received`.
2. The request is queued; a worker moves it to `rendering`.
3. `RenderService` resolves the active template and renders the PDF.
4. `SignatureService` seals the PDF.
5. `StorageService` uploads it and writes the `documents` row.
6. The request moves to `rendered`.

context.heading: Boundaries
context.content:
Billing Core owns subscriptions, invoices, payment attempts and refunds. It does
not own user identity: it stores `user_id` as an opaque reference and resolves
display data from the identity service when a human-readable invoice is needed.

answer:
Finisce su S3, sotto la chiave `documents/{tenantId}/{documentId}.pdf`, e solo `StorageService` tocca il client S3 [02-architecture.md — Storage].

Nel flusso, dopo il render il PDF viene sigillato da `SignatureService` e poi caricato da `StorageService`, che scrive la riga in `documents` [05-main-flows.md — Document production flow]. La riga contiene `id`, `request_id`, `storage_key`, `checksum_sha256`, `signed`, `size_bytes`, `created_at` [03-data-model.md — documents].

Le chiavi degli oggetti non vengono mai riusate: un nuovo render produce un nuovo document id [02-architecture.md — Storage].

question: Quando una consegna viene ritentata?

context.heading: Delivery errors
context.content:
Provider errors are normalised to `provider_rejected`, `provider_unavailable`
and `recipient_invalid`. `recipient_invalid` is final. `provider_unavailable` is
retryable. `provider_rejected` is retryable only when the provider marks the
error code as retryable.

context.heading: Billing routes
context.content:
`/v1/invoices/*` and `/v1/subscriptions/*` forward to the `billing-core`
upstream and require the caller to carry a billing scope.

context.heading: Timeouts
context.content:
`upstreamTimeoutMs` is the default upstream timeout and is 30000. A route can
override it with its own `timeoutMs`. `readHeaderTimeoutMs` is 5000 and
`idleTimeoutMs` is 120000.

context.heading: Database settings
context.content:
`DATABASE_URL` is the Postgres connection string. `DB_POOL_SIZE` defaults to 10
connections per replica. `DB_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS` defaults to 5000 and is
applied per statement by the pool.

context.heading: Retry flow
context.content:
A delivery in `rejected` state is retried only if the provider reported a
retryable error code. Retries create a new `deliveries` row with an incremented
`attempt_number`. A `bounced` delivery is never retried.

context.heading: deliveries
context.content:
`deliveries` holds `id`, `document_id`, `provider`, `recipient`, `status`,
`provider_message_id`, `error_code`, `attempt_number`, `created_at`,
`updated_at`. `status` is one of `queued`, `sent`, `accepted`, `rejected`,
`bounced`.

context.heading: Domain errors
context.content:
`invoice_not_draft` (HTTP 409) when issuing a non-draft invoice.
`invoice_not_payable` (HTTP 409) when charging an invoice that is not `open`.
`refund_exceeds_amount` (HTTP 422) when the refund amount is larger than the
paid amount.

answer:
Solo in base al codice di errore riportato dal provider.

- Una delivery in stato `rejected` viene ritentata soltanto se il provider ha riportato un codice di errore retryable; i retry creano una nuova riga in `deliveries` con `attempt_number` incrementato [05-main-flows.md — Retry flow].
- Una delivery `bounced` non viene mai ritentata [05-main-flows.md — Retry flow].
- Sul lato errori: `recipient_invalid` è definitivo, `provider_unavailable` è retryable e `provider_rejected` è retryable solo quando il provider marca il codice come retryable [07-errors.md — Delivery errors].

Gli stati possibili di una delivery sono `queued`, `sent`, `accepted`, `rejected`, `bounced` [03-data-model.md — deliveries].

question: Come funziona la firma dei documenti?

context.content:
Configuration is read at boot by `config/loadConfig.ts`. Values come from

context.heading: SignatureService
context.content:

4. `SignatureService` seals the PDF.
5. `StorageService` uploads it and writes the `documents` row.
6. The request moves to `rendered`.

context.heading: Deployment
context.content:

question: Qual è la differenza tra document request, document e delivery?

context.heading: Current User Flow
context.content:

context.content:

a provider. One document can have several deliveries.

context.heading: AuthService
context.content:
`AuthService` verifies credentials, issues access and refresh tokens and
revokes sessions. It depends on `UserRepository` to load the account and on

pair loaded at boot from the secret store.

context.heading: Default upstream timeout

The platform timeout policy sets the default upstream timeout to 10000 ms. Mesh

context.heading: document_requests
context.content:
`document_requests` holds `id`, `tenant_id`, `template_code`, `payload_json`,
`channel`, `status`, `created_at`. `status` is one of `received`, `rendering`,
`render_failed`, `rendered`, `delivering`, `delivered`, `failed`.

context.heading: Error envelope
context.content:
Every error response uses `{ "error": "<code>", "message": "<human text>" }`.
The `error` code is stable and safe to switch on; `message` is not.

context.heading: documents
context.content:
`documents` holds `id`, `request_id`, `storage_key`, `checksum_sha256`,
`signed`, `size_bytes`, `created_at`. One row per successfully rendered
artefact.

answer:
Sono tre entità distinte con cardinalità diverse [01-overview.md — Vocabulary]:

- Una *document request* è ciò che il chiamante invia; è tracciata in `document_requests` con `template_code`, `payload_json`, `channel` e uno stato tra `received`, `rendering`, `render_failed`, `rendered`, `delivering`, `delivered`, `failed` [01-overview.md — Vocabulary] [03-data-model.md — document_requests].
- Un *document* è l'artefatto renderizzato, una riga in `documents` per ogni render riuscito [01-overview.md — Vocabulary] [03-data-model.md — documents].
- Una *delivery* è un singolo tentativo di consegna a un destinatario tramite un provider, e un documento può averne diverse [01-overview.md — Vocabulary].

question: Which component talks to S3?

question: Come si passa da uno stato received a uno stato delivered?

context.heading: Login Flow
context.content:
1. `POST /auth/login` reaches `AuthController.login`.
2. `AuthService.authenticate` loads the account by email via `UserRepository`.
3. The password is verified against `password_hash` with argon2id.
4. On success `AuthService` issues an access token and a refresh token, and
   stores the refresh token hash through `SessionRepository.create`.

context.heading: Document production flow
context.content:
1. `POST /documents` stores a `document_requests` row with status `received`.
2. The request is queued; a worker moves it to `rendering`.
3. `RenderService` resolves the active template and renders the PDF.
4. `SignatureService` seals the PDF.
5. `StorageService` uploads it and writes the `documents` row.
6. The request moves to `rendered`.

context.heading: Delivery flow
context.content:
1. Once the request is `rendered`, `DeliveryService.deliver` is invoked.
2. `ProviderRouter` resolves the channel to a provider bean.
3. The provider is called; a `deliveries` row is written with status `queued`
   before the call and updated to `sent` when the provider accepts it.
4. The provider later calls `POST /providers/callbacks/{provider}`.
5. `DeliveryStatusListener` updates the delivery to `accepted`, `rejected` or
   `bounced`.

context.heading: POST /invoices/{id}/issue
context.content:
Moves an invoice from `draft` to `open`, assigns the invoice `number`, renders
the PDF and enqueues the first payment attempt. Returns HTTP 202. Issuing is
rejected with HTTP 409 `invoice_not_draft` if the invoice is not in `draft`.

context.heading: POST /invoices
context.content:
Creates a draft invoice for a subscription. Body: `{ subscriptionId, lines }`.
Returns HTTP 201 with the invoice in `draft` status. Creating an invoice does
not charge anything.

context.heading: Upstream errors
context.content:
`upstream_timeout` (HTTP 504) when the upstream exceeds the route timeout.
`upstream_unavailable` (HTTP 502) when the connection fails. The gateway never
converts an upstream 5xx into a 2xx: upstream status codes above 499 are passed
through unchanged, with the body replaced by the gateway error envelope.

context.heading: document_requests
context.content:
`document_requests` holds `id`, `tenant_id`, `template_code`, `payload_json`,
`channel`, `status`, `created_at`. `status` is one of `received`, `rendering`,
`render_failed`, `rendered`, `delivering`, `delivered`, `failed`.

answer:
Gli stati previsti per una richiesta sono `received`, `rendering`, `render_failed`, `rendered`, `delivering`, `delivered`, `failed` [03-data-model.md — document_requests].

Percorso documentato:
1. `POST /documents` salva la riga con stato `received`; la richiesta viene messa in coda e un worker la porta in `rendering` [05-main-flows.md — Document production flow].
2. `RenderService` risolve il template attivo e produce il PDF, `SignatureService` lo sigilla, `StorageService` lo carica e scrive la riga in `documents`; la richiesta passa a `rendered` [05-main-flows.md — Document production flow].
3. Una volta `rendered` viene invocata `DeliveryService.deliver`; `ProviderRouter` risolve il canale, il provider viene chiamato e la riga in `deliveries` passa da `queued` a `sent` [05-main-flows.md — Delivery flow].
4. Il provider richiama `POST /providers/callbacks/{provider}` e `DeliveryStatusListener` aggiorna la delivery ad `accepted`, `rejected` o `bounced` [05-main-flows.md — Delivery flow].

context.heading: Purpose
context.content:
Mesh Gateway is the single ingress for every public API call at Acme. It is a Go
service that terminates TLS, authenticates the caller, applies rate limits and
forwards the request to the right upstream service. It holds no business logic

the invoice in `draft`.

context.content:
`upstreamTimeoutMs` is the default upstream timeout and is 30000. A route can
override it with its own `timeoutMs`. `readHeaderTimeoutMs` is 5000 and
`idleTimeoutMs` is 120000.

context.heading: Deployment
context.content:
The service runs as two workloads from the same image: the HTTP API and the

and share the same configuration.

context.content:

enforced by the server, not by the gateway.

context.content:
`deliveries` holds `id`, `document_id`, `provider`, `recipient`, `status`,
`provider_message_id`, `error_code`, `attempt_number`, `created_at`,
`updated_at`. `status` is one of `queued`, `sent`, `accepted`, `rejected`,

context.content:

La documentazione fornita è contrastante su questo valore.

context.content:

context.content:

context.content:

context.content:

HTTP 504 con codice `upstream_timeout`, quando l'upstream supera il timeout della rotta [06-errors.md — Upstream errors].

question: Come vengono risolte le rotte?

context.heading: RouteResolver
context.content:
`RouteResolver` matches the request path against the route table and produces an
upstream target. The route table is loaded from `routes.yaml` at startup and
refreshed on SIGHUP. An unmatched path returns HTTP 404 `route_not_found`
without contacting any upstream.

context.heading: Channel routing
context.content:
`docsync.channels` maps a channel name to a provider bean name, for example
`email: emailDeliveryProvider`. A channel absent from this map is unsupported at
runtime.

context.heading: Authentication flow
context.content:
Every protected route passes through `authMiddleware`. The middleware reads the
`Authorization: Bearer <token>` header, verifies the RS256 signature, checks the
`exp` claim and loads the account id from the `sub` claim. It then attaches
`req.auth = { userId, scopes }`. Routes never parse the token themselves.

context.heading: POST /webhooks/stripe
context.content:
Receives Stripe callbacks. The route verifies the Stripe signature header
before doing anything else, stores the raw event in `webhook_events` and returns
HTTP 200 immediately. Processing happens asynchronously in `billing-worker`.

context.heading: routes.yaml
context.content:
Each entry declares `path`, `methods`, `upstream`, `timeoutMs`, `authRequired`
and `rateLimit`. The first matching entry wins, so more specific paths must be
declared before wildcards.

context.heading: sessions table
context.content:
The `sessions` table holds refresh tokens: `id`, `user_id`, `refresh_token_hash`,
`user_agent`, `expires_at`, `revoked_at`. Access tokens are never stored; only
refresh tokens are persisted, and only as a hash.

answer:
`RouteResolver` confronta il path della richiesta con la route table e produce un target upstream. La tabella viene caricata da `routes.yaml` all'avvio e ricaricata su SIGHUP; un path senza corrispondenza restituisce HTTP 404 `route_not_found` senza contattare nessun upstream [02-architecture.md — RouteResolver].

Ogni voce di `routes.yaml` dichiara `path`, `methods`, `upstream`, `timeoutMs`, `authRequired` e `rateLimit`, e vince la prima corrispondenza: i path più specifici vanno dichiarati prima dei wildcard [03-routing.md — routes.yaml].

question: Perché il rate limiter usa Redis?

context.heading: Kubernetes
context.content:
The gateway is deployed as a Deployment with 4 replicas and a HorizontalPodAutoscaler
targeting 60% CPU. The Service is of type LoadBalancer. Config is mounted from
the `mesh-gateway-config` ConfigMap; `routes.yaml` lives in the same ConfigMap.

context.heading: Database settings
context.content:
`DATABASE_URL` is the Postgres connection string. `DB_POOL_SIZE` defaults to 10
connections per replica. `DB_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS` defaults to 5000 and is
applied per statement by the pool.

context.heading: Loading
context.content:
Configuration is a pydantic `Settings` object in `billing/config.py`, populated
from environment variables. Unknown variables are ignored; missing required
variables abort startup.

context.heading: RateLimiter
context.content:
`RateLimiter` is a token bucket keyed by caller id and route. Buckets live in
Redis so all gateway replicas share the same budget. When the bucket is empty
the request is rejected with HTTP 429 and a `Retry-After` header.

context.heading: AuthService
context.content:
`AuthService` verifies credentials, issues access and refresh tokens and
revokes sessions. It depends on `UserRepository` to load the account and on
`SessionRepository` to persist refresh tokens. Token signing uses the RS256 key
pair loaded at boot from the secret store.

context.heading: Purpose
context.content:
Acme Identity is the internal service that owns user accounts, profiles and
session tokens for every Acme product. It is a TypeScript service running on
Node 20 and exposes a REST API behind the internal gateway. All other services
treat it as the single source of truth for "who is this user".

answer:
Perché il budget deve essere condiviso fra le repliche: `RateLimiter` è un token bucket per caller id e rotta, e i bucket vivono in Redis proprio perché tutte le repliche del gateway condividano lo stesso budget. Quando il bucket è vuoto la richiesta viene rifiutata con HTTP 429 e un header `Retry-After` [02-architecture.md — RateLimiter].

Il gateway è effettivamente multi-replica: è deployato come Deployment con 4 repliche e un HorizontalPodAutoscaler al 60% di CPU [07-deployment.md — Kubernetes].
